panels.description:
Current instance count per project across the selected hypervisors (oie_instance_info).

Source: OIE inventory/mapping metrics emitted by the exporter (instance/project/user labels derived on the hypervisor).
Limitations: Reflects what OIE can map at collection time; labels can be temporarily stale during rebuilds/migrations or if OpenStack metadata is unavailable. Counts are not traffic-based.

Project ranking controls: Top Projects limits which projects are shown in this panel. 0 (All) shows every matching project. Rank Projects By uses the visible time range: Last = right-edge value, Max = highest value in range, Mean = average value in range. For multi-series panels, the project selection is based on the panel's primary series and the matching companion series for those same projects are shown.
panels.title: Instance Count by Project

panels.description:
Total RAM allocated per project in MiB (sum of assigned memory across all instances on selected hypervisors).

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE (plus derived scoring).
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. RAM allocation is provisioned/configured (scheduler/accounting), not guest 'used'. Clouds may overcommit RAM (e.g., allocation ratios), and this excludes some host overhead.

Project ranking controls: Top Projects limits which projects are shown in this panel. 0 (All) shows every matching project. Rank Projects By uses the visible time range: Last = right-edge value, Max = highest value in range, Mean = average value in range. For multi-series panels, the project selection is based on the panel's primary series and the matching companion series for those same projects are shown.

targets.expr:
(sum by (project_uuid, project_name) (
  label_replace(
    oie_instance_mem_allocated_mb{job="openstack-instance-exporter", instance=~"^${gvar_oie_hypervisor}(:[0-9]+)?$", project_uuid=~"$gvar_oie_project_uuid",             project_name=~"$gvar_oie_project_name" },
    "mem_mb_num",
    "$1",
    "mem_mb",
    "([0-9]+)"

Aggregate host-scheduler runqueue delay across VM vCPUs in each project, in vCPU-seconds per wall-clock second. Libvirt delay/steal is preferred per vCPU and wait is used only as a compatibility fallback; the two aliases are never added.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU vCPU delay and wait counters collected by OIE.
Limitations: Counters can reset on VM reboot or migration; short rate windows can be spiky.

Project ranking controls: Top Projects limits which projects are shown. Rank Projects By uses the visible time range.

targets.expr:
(sum by (project_uuid, project_name) (
  rate(oie_instance_cpu_steal_seconds_total{job="openstack-instance-exporter", instance=~"^${gvar_oie_hypervisor}(:[0-9]+)?$", project_uuid=~"$gvar_oie_project_uuid", project_name=~"$gvar_oie_project_name"}[1m])
  or
  rate(oie_instance_cpu_wait_seconds_total{job="openstack-instance-exporter", instance=~"^${gvar_oie_hypervisor}(:[0-9]+)?$", project_uuid=~"$gvar_oie_project_uuid", project_name=~"$gvar_oie_project_name"}[1m])
))
and on(project_uuid, project_name)
topk(${gvar_oie_top_projects}, ${gvar_oie_rank_projects_by:raw}(((sum by (project_uuid, project_name) (
  rate(oie_instance_cpu_steal_seconds_total{job="openstack-instance-exporter", instance=~"^${gvar_oie_hypervisor}(:[0-9]+)?$", project_uuid=~"$gvar_oie_project_uuid", project_name=~"$gvar_oie_project_name"}[1m])

)))[${__range_s}s:] @ end()))

panels.title: CPU Efficiency (Used/Allocated %)

panels.description:
Reported guest-visible logical disk sizes, grouped by the existing disk_type label. That label contains a source type or pool name; it does not reliably identify the storage backend. In particular, local means a file source in the existing exporter label and does not prove local physical storage. A pool name alone does not prove RBD.

This is provisioned address space for observed disk attachments, not used bytes, free space, guest-filesystem usage, or physical backend consumption. A shared disk can be counted once per observed attachment. Missing capacity observations are omitted; absent or unreachable hosts are not a complete inventory. Capacity remains visible when the optional highest-written-offset field is unavailable. Use Ceph-native telemetry for authoritative backend consumption.

The existing paired capacity/offset view is available in the collapsed Disk address-space diagnostics row.

Top Projects selects projects by their total reported logical capacity using the selected Last, Max or Mean ranking; source type/pool series for the selected projects are then shown. 0 (All) includes every matching project.

panels.title: Configured Allocation Minus Guest-View Used (MiB)

panels.description: Retype monitoring is off by default; explicitly enable it in OIE to populate this table. Active and recently completed Cinder RBD volume retypes for the selected project scope, observed through Libvirt block-copy state. Scope: this compute-local view covers only volumes attached to active Libvirt domains on hosts scraped by OIE. Detached or available-volume retypes run within Cinder or the storage backend and have no compute-side Libvirt block job, so they are not visible here. OIE does not query Cinder; Cinder remains authoritative for migration status and lifecycle timestamps. Root/boot volumes are included when Libvirt exposes a matching job; their retype support and outcome still depend on the OpenStack and storage path. Source RBD Pool and Destination RBD Pool are parsed from the saved RBD image names; they are not Cinder volume-type names. Source RBD Image and Destination RBD Image are RBD image basenames that retain the volume- prefix; strip that prefix before passing either value to openstack volume show. Once a job is known, the completion-paced fast poller inspects mirror XML no more often than every 5 seconds, with the interval beginning after the preceding attempt completes. Block-job progress is queried no more often than every 15 seconds after the preceding query completes and waits 30 seconds after a failed query completes before retrying. Initial discovery remains bounded to 256 domain XML reads per exporter collection cycle and still runs during normal collections when no retype is known; only the idle fast-poller and block-job paths make no Libvirt calls. All lifecycle fields for one retained operation are merged into one table row. If the exact same source/destination identity is observed repeatedly on one instance disk, only its newest retained row is kept. Status 1 means copying is in progress. Status 5 means Libvirt reports the copy ready and awaiting pivot; this is non-terminal and does not prove Cinder success. Status 6 means that copy-ready state has remained for at least 10 minutes since this exporter first observed it and requires operator attention. Status 2 means a successful terminal XML inspection found the destination as the live source. Status 3 means that inspection found the original source, which can represent a failed or cancelled operation. Status 4 is emitted only when a successful XML inspection finds the mirror gone but cannot match the final live source to the saved source or destination. A job that merely becomes too old to reconfirm expires without a terminal status, row, timestamp, or result-counter increment. Libvirt Observation is Healthy when the latest block-job information query succeeded and Unavailable when that query failed; the per-job observation and progress fields are omitted while the main Libvirt source is unavailable; it is not a statement about the Nova or Cinder outcome. Libvirt Job Present remains Yes for copying, copy-ready, and ready-stalled jobs until the job is pivoted or aborted. First Observed, Copy Ready Observed, and Terminal Observed are exporter observation timestamps, not authoritative Cinder API lifecycle timestamps. Recent rows, timestamps, and result counters are in-memory exporter-process state and reset on exporter restart. A terminal row is retained for one hour, with at most 256 retained rows per exporter, and then disappears; Prometheus historical retention remains independent. Logical progress is Libvirt/QEMU's approximate cur/end position across the block job's logical work range, not Ceph physical allocation, transferred bytes, or an ETA. Thin-provisioned or sparse regions and regions discarded by guest fstrim/TRIM, when discard propagated to RBD, can require little or no data transfer, so progress is not time-linear and retyping can finish sooner than percentage extrapolation suggests. Progress is omitted when Libvirt has no usable current total or the latest query failed, except that copy-ready XML independently proves the logical copy phase reached 100%. An empty table can mean no matching observations or unavailable telemetry; check the visible coverage indicators.
